prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create actual newly illustrated 2D game animation frame artwork, not a preview board. The supplied PNG is the approved character design and painting style reference, not an image to rotate, scale, squash, warp or reuse as a cutout. Draw every pose afresh with coherent anatomy, newly drawn contours, material surfaces and lighting appropriate to that pose. Polished soft hand-painted 2D sprite shading, fine dark teal outline, warm upper-left light, exactly match the reference palette and visual finish. One sprite sheet only: exactly 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 equal square cells, read left to right then top to bottom. Requested output 2048x2048 pixels. Genuinely transparent background, NO checkerboard drawing, NO scene, ground, backdrop, shadows, labels, letters, numbers, grid lines, cell borders, glow or extra characters. No object crosses its cell boundary. Fixed camera, fixed drawing scale and fixed ground baseline at 88% of each cell. On the first frame the character is centered horizontally, full neutral visible height about 60% of a cell, from 28% to 88%; keep its mass and scale consistent, let only the actual death action change its silhouette. This is a one-shot DEATH followed by still remains, never return to life. Design the intervening drawings as sequential animation poses, not sixteen unrelated variations. All 16 cells must contain the same recognizable character at successive moments of the action. Character: the reference coral mushroom, broad heavy coral-pink cap, cream short stalk body, two tiny cream feet and two dark teal eyes. Preserve the particular broad sloping cap shape, its broad mauve underside and subtle gills. Death action: the stalk loses strength and bends sideways, then the heavy cap drops late, folds softly and flops onto its side over the stalk. This must look like newly drawn organic buckling and a folding cloth-like cap, NOT a rotated or flattened copy of a standing mushroom. Show newly exposed underside as the cap tips, a curled rim, and a curved limp stalk with realistic overlap. Row 1 frames 1-4: exact-design standing neutral, eyelids lowering, knees/stalk weakening, stalk curving to the right while cap initially stays upright and heavy. Row 2 frames 5-8: stalk folds further; cap lags left and then tips downward to the right, its right rim begins to curl and folds. Row 3 frames 9-12: the heavy asymmetric cap falls, its underside newly drawn in perspective; it lands on its right rim and slumps over the bent stalk, feet resting without a jump. Row 4 frames 13-16: one short cap flap after contact, then settle into a low, clearly lifeless mushroom heap, the slanted folded cap covering almost the whole sideways stalk, one tiny cream foot visible. The last two drawings are almost settled with slightly different rim settling, final one completely at rest. Eyes closed early, hidden under cap at end. Keep it cute and tender, no blood, no magic, no particles. Clear action silhouette, volumetric cap folds, smooth continuity.
